answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: each agent account accrues influence only as the product of account age and completed honest epochs, so influence grows on a delta curve no money can flatten. A falcon-style fast operator spawning a juniper forest of fresh identities gains almost nothing, since a new account acts at near-zero weight for months. Attack cost equals paying per fake identity while earning negligible output during the entire maturation period, making bulk sybils unprofitable.
